thread:
Maria (PM): Heads-up: enterprise legal pushed a draft clause asking for a 99.9% "successful token emission" SLA for Dedicated and Private. We need to decide GA position and mitigations.
Ethan (Eng): 99.9% token-level is achievable but not without infra and cost changes. we should be explicit about measurement window and exclusions.
Oliver (DevEx): measurement suggestion: rolling 30d "successful_token_rate" measured per-customer, calculated as tokens_returned / tokens_requested. exclude scheduled maintenance and customer-side misconfig.
Priya (Support): support implications: need a published runbook linking metric breaches -> remediation steps -> customer comms. L2 must have a short checklist and a template message.
FinOps Bot: estimated impact for Dedicated (reserved pools): +10-14% committed GPU hours if we provision warm pools + pre-pull. will produce a per-commitment table.
Ethan (Eng): concrete mitigations: 1) warm pools (baseline kept warm) 2) prepull on deploy and model-switch events 3) fallback model chain (primary -> quantized warmed variant -> cached prefix -> explicit 503 with ETA). fallback policy must be documented as part of SLA.
Maria (PM): can we phrase SLA to promise degradation behavior rather than hard zero-failure? e.g., guarantee 99.9% successful_token_rate, and in rare cases we provide fallback with explained behavior.
Oliver (DevEx): draft wording idea: "Successful token emission rate >= 99.9% over a 30-day rolling window per-customer. In the event of service degradation, Redwood will attempt automated fallbacks (listed) before returning an error; fallback responses may have reduced model fidelity. Exclusions: customer network issues, misuse, DDoS, scheduled maintenance >= 4h per month."
Ethan (Eng): to meet that we need autoscale config change and a warmed reserve. sample autoscale override: 
```yaml
reserved_capacity: 100
warm_pool_percent: 0.12 # 12% warm baseline to reduce cold starts
prepull_on_deploy: true
```
Ethan (Eng): cost note: warm_pool_percent translates to ~12% additional GPU-hours. Private customers on their own infra: we provide recommended config but can't enforce costs.
Priya (Support): runbook elements: detection (alert when 30d rolling < 99.95%), quick triage steps, escalate to SRE, customer notification templates (initial + 24h follow-up), and SLA credit calculation steps. need an owner and two backups.
Maria (PM): owners: Ethan -> infra changes + cost model; Oliver -> SLA doc + dashboard spec; Priya -> runbook + comms; FinOps -> pricing uplift proposal. Drafts due Tue EOD, review Wed, leadership sign-off Thurs.
FinOps Bot: pricing options: (A) flat uplift +12% to committed price; (B) tiered SLA: default 99.5% at base price, 99.9% as paid premium; (C) line-item for warm-pool. I'll output a sample table.
Oliver (DevEx): Console feature ask: expose a per-customer "SLA health" metric, CSV export for compliance, and a 90/180/365 day history chart so customers can verify. reduces support friction.
SRE Bot: note: scheduling canary for warm-pool change at 1755001250 on 3% capacity. watch model_fallback_count and token_success_ratio.
Ethan (Eng): canary watchlist: model_fallback_count, kv_cache_evictions, p99 tail latency. I'll add temporary extra tracing in canary rollout.
Priya (Support): I'll run a 20-min L2 walkthrough Fri to cover runbook scenarios and customer comms.
Maria (PM): recap action items: Ethan -> autoscale config + cost delta + canary plan; Oliver -> SLA legal-ready draft + Console spec + export format; Priya -> runbook + notification templates; FinOps -> pricing options table. All review Wed. Any blocking concerns?
Ethan (Eng): main risk = customers pushing for contractual uptime without accepting cost uplift. recommend we push tiered SLA option.
Maria (PM): good. Oliver, include tiered SLA language in the draft. Thanks team.
